# The United States Medical Licensing Examination® (USMLE)

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > The United States Medical Licensing Examination® (USMLE)*

[Original Article Link](/library/aJ0QsS)

---

## Summary

The United States Medical Licensing Examination<sup>®</sup> (USMLE) is a three-step assessment program that evaluates medical students and physicians intending to practice medicine in the United States. Sponsored by the Federation of State Medical Boards<sup>®</sup> (FSMB) and the <u>National Board of Medical Examiners<sup>®</sup></u> (<u>NBME</u>), the USMLE assesses an individual's ability to apply their medical knowledge and demonstrate fundamental <u>patient-centered</u> skills. Passing the USMLE is required for physicians with a Doctor of Medicine (MD) degree for medical licensure, and for <u>international medical graduates</u> (<u>IMGs</u>) for Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates<sup>®</sup> (ECFMG) certification, which enables them to enter residency or fellowship programs in the US that are accredited by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME). The USMLE is not required for those with a Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine degree (DO), but over 60% also take at least <u>USMLE Step 1</u>, in addition to their required licensure exam, the <u>Comprehensive Osteopathic Medical Licensing Examination</u> of the United States<sup>®</sup>, or <u>COMLEX</u>.




The USMLE is split into three distinct steps in the form of computerized examinations. <u>Step 1</u> tests the examinee's foundational understanding of the basic sciences, including anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, and pharmacology, all of which are typically integrated with pathology. <u>Step 2 Clinical Knowledge</u> (CK) focuses on the clinical sciences and the application of this knowledge to patient care under supervision. The <u>Step 2 Clinical Skills</u> (CS), which examined an examinee's communication and patient care skills through simulated patient encounters, was discontinued in 2021. Finally, Step 3 assesses the ability to independently understand and apply medical knowledge in an unsupervised clinical setting, with a focus on patient management in outpatient settings.
